findings.evidence: Scripts: for a prerequisite check, read and run `scripts/check-tool.sh <tool> [install-command]`
findings.fix: Keep the one-line pointer, but drop the separate 'read and run' instruction: the script's --help already documents usage, so the agent should run it rather than also loading the source. Record the removed words in docs/audit/recovery/dependency-updater/record.md.

findings.evidence: The body is a nine-step process with checkpoints, but the Node path then offers three ways to write the same cohort.
findings.fix: Keep the process pattern. In the Node bullet, state one default (edit the approved target versions in the manifest, then resolve with the owning manager) and move the disposable-copy taze write to references/node.md as the only escape hatch, named once.

findings.evidence: `taze minor --write --include <the scanned candidate names>` is the auto-apply write, with no rule for a cohort that is only patches.
findings.fix: Add one gotcha: when the auto-apply cohort is patches only, `taze minor` also writes minors, so use `taze patch --write --include <names> --no-github-actions --no-node-version` (or edit the manifest) and compare the diff to the target map. Cite `taze --help` as the live mode list.

findings.evidence: The Node bullet repeats the disposable-copy taze command, the `--include` rule and the GitHub Actions side effect that references/node.md already states.
findings.fix: Leave in SKILL.md only the default (edit the manifest), the NEVER about a write-mode taze without `--include`, and 'Load node.md only for a Node manifest'. Keep the flag procedure solely in references/node.md.

findings.evidence: The default scoped write is editing the target versions directly in the manifest. The alternatives run only in a disposable copy of the project: for the auto-apply cohort `taze minor --write --include ...`
findings.fix: Name one default for a Node write: edit the exact target versions in the manifest and resolve with the owning manager. Mention the disposable-copy `taze minor`/`taze major` write once, in references/node.md, as the escape hatch when hand-editing ranges is the harder path.

findings.evidence: All eight evals are Node or Poetry plans; none supplies a Go, Cargo, Bundler, Maven or .NET fixture, and the trigger set has 11 should-trigger queries against 10 should-not-trigger.
findings.fix: Add one eval whose prompt and files are a Go module or a Cargo project, asserting the exact approved-target command from references/managers.md (`go get module@version` then `go mod tidy`, or `cargo update -p crate --precise version`) and that a broad upgrade-all is refused. Move one easy negative trigger query out so the two sides are 10 and 10.

findings.evidence: `taze minor --write --include <the scanned candidate names>` is the write for the auto-apply cohort, which the policy defines as both MINOR and PATCH.
findings.fix: Say that `taze minor` may raise a patch-only package to its latest minor, so a patch-only cohort uses `taze patch --write --include <names> --no-github-actions --no-node-version` (or a direct manifest edit), and the copy's diff is still compared to the package-to-exact-target map before anything is copied back.

findings.evidence: Confirm the repository's manager from lockfiles/workspace configuration (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, or Yarn lock/config`); do not generate a competing lockfile.
findings.fix: Add the tie-break: when both `package-lock.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` (or a Yarn lock) exist, the manager is the one named in `packageManager` or the repo's documented install command; if neither says, stop and ask instead of picking one and generating its lockfile.
